name: Evaluating Agents and Reinforcement Learning in Real Settings
gist: Papers test AI agents trying to solve actual problems like cybersecurity, power systems, travel planning, or video game strategy — measuring whether they can act in complex real-world scenarios.
explain: An agent is a system that takes actions over time to solve a problem. It might be an AI playing a game, a robot trying to pick up an object, a program trying to defend against a cyberattack, or a planner booking flights and hotels to get you somewhere. Testing an agent is not like testing a model that just answers one question. You have to simulate a whole sequence of decisions and see whether the agent reaches its goal. This subtheme is about building environments and benchmarks where researchers can measure how well agents learn and act.

The difficulty is that real-world agent problems have delays, surprises, and cascading consequences. If an agent makes a mistake, the world changes in ways it has to recover from. If it is learning, it might be exploring and failing over and over before figuring things out. Benchmarks have to test both: can the agent learn from trial and error (the classic reinforcement learning problem), and can it handle the kind of complex, long-term planning humans face? A power grid agent has to keep the system stable while responding to outages; a travel planner has to route through real constraints (weather, prices, time zones); a cybersecurity agent has to detect and respond to attacks in a realistic network. Each domain has its own twists that make simple simulation tests inadequate.

The papers in this area build two kinds of testing environments. Some create detailed simulators of real domains—power grids, network security, travel booking—where agents can be trained and tested without real-world risk. Others propose metrics that measure not just whether an agent succeeded, but how well it adapted, whether it learned over time, and whether it handled the unexpected. The goal is to move from testing agents on toy problems to testing them on problem-spaces that feel like the real world.

papers.title: Accelerating Benchmarking of Functional Connectivity Modeling via Structure-aware Core-set Selection
papers.contribution: Preserves ground-truth model ranking with just 10% of data, outperforming state-of-the-art core-set selection by up to 23.2% in ranking consistency.

papers.title: Benchmarking Open-ended Segmentation
papers.contribution: Presents first Multi-modal LLM trained with contrastive objective for jointly aligning visual regions and textual descriptions, achieving state-of-the-art results.

papers.title: DAComp: Benchmarking Data Agents across the Full Data Intelligence Lifecycle
papers.contribution: State-of-the-art agents achieve under 10% success on DE tasks and below 40% on DA tasks, revealing that holistic pipeline orchestration and open-ended reasoning are distinct critical bottlenecks, not mere code generation challenges.

papers.title: DiscoX: Benchmarking Discourse-Level Translation in Expert Domains
papers.contribution: DiscoX reveals a performance gap where even advanced LLMs trail human experts on professional-grade translation and provides a rigorous framework for evaluating discourse-level translation.

papers.title: InnoGym: Benchmarking the Innovation Potential of AI Agents
papers.contribution: Framework and unified execution environment (iGym) reveal gap between creativity and effectiveness: agents produce novel approaches but lack robustness for consistent performance gains.

papers.title: LiveResearchBench: Benchmarking Single- and Multi-Agent Systems for Citation-Grounded Deep Research
papers.contribution: The benchmark enables rigorous evaluation of frontier deep research systems including single-agent and multi-agent approaches, revealing current strengths and failure modes.

papers.title: LogiConBench: Benchmarking Logical Consistencies of LLMs
papers.contribution: Provides 280K scalable samples remaining challenging for frontier LLMs; the Enumerative task achieves only 34% exact accuracy for the best model, establishing a robust benchmark.

papers.title: PepBenchmark: A Standardized Benchmark for Peptide Machine Learning
papers.contribution: Provides first standardized and comparable foundation for peptide drug discovery, facilitating methodological advances and translation to real-world applications.

papers.title: SimBench: Benchmarking the Ability of Large Language Models to Simulate Human Behaviors
papers.contribution: Shows best LLMs have limited simulation ability (40.80/100), performance scales log-linearly with model size, and simulation correlates with deep reasoning (MMLU-Pro r=0.939).

papers.title: SparseEval: Efficient Evaluation of Large Language Models by Sparse Optimization
papers.contribution: SparseEval demonstrates low estimation error and high Kendall's tau across benchmarks, showcasing superior robustness and practicality for efficient LLM evaluation in real-world scenarios.

papers.title: SpeechJudge: Towards Human-Level Judgment for Speech Naturalness
papers.contribution: SpeechJudge-GRM achieves 77.2% accuracy on the SpeechJudge-Eval benchmark, substantially improving over existing metrics and AudioLLMs.

papers.title: A Statistical Benchmark for Diffusion Posterior Sampling Algorithms
papers.contribution: Enables arbitrary-precision Monte Carlo estimation and isolation of algorithmic errors from learned component errors across multiple inverse problems.

papers.title: AICrypto: Evaluating Cryptography Capabilities of Large Language Models
papers.contribution: State-of-the-art models match or exceed human experts in memorization and vulnerability exploitation but struggle with abstract mathematical concepts and multi-step dynamic reasoning.

papers.title: AMemGym: Interactive Memory Benchmarking for Assistants in Long-Horizon Conversations
papers.contribution: Reveals performance gaps in existing memory systems (RAG, long-context LLMs, agentic memory) and enables diagnostically rich assessment of memory management.

papers.title: Agent-X: Evaluating Deep Multimodal Reasoning in Vision-Centric Agentic Tasks
papers.contribution: Reveals even best-performing models (GPT, Gemini, Qwen families) achieve less than 50% full-chain success on multi-step vision tasks, identifying key reasoning and tool-use bottlenecks.

papers.title: AnesSuite: A Comprehensive Benchmark and Dataset Suite for Anesthesiology Reasoning in LLMs
papers.contribution: Morpheus demonstrates substantial performance improvements rivaling larger-scale models despite limited training, and analysis reveals key factors influencing anesthesiology reasoning performance.

papers.title: AudioTrust: Benchmarking The Multifaceted Trustworthiness of Audio Large Language Models
papers.contribution: Comprehensive evaluation of 14 SOTA ALLMs reveals vulnerabilities to diverse high-risk audio scenarios, offering critical insights for secure deployment.

papers.title: Aurelius: Relation Aware Text-to-Audio Generation At Scale
papers.contribution: We further provide in-depth investigation on scaling up existing TTA models' relation aware generation by either training from scratch or leveraging cross-domain general TTA knowledge

papers.title: AutoBaxBuilder: Bootstrapping Code Security Benchmarking
papers.contribution: AutoBaxBuilder generates new security tasks in under 2 hours for less than $4 USD, reducing human effort by 12×; quality aligns with expert-written baselines.

papers.title: BEST: Benchmarking Efficiency in Space and Time for LLM-Generated Code
papers.contribution: Demonstrates LLMs exhibit weak time-efficiency and even weaker space-efficiency capabilities through extensive experiments across 50 LLMs; reveals critical gaps in efficient code synthesis.

papers.title: Benchmarking Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning in Power Grid Operations
papers.contribution: Current MARL methods struggle under real-world conditions, revealing coordination and constraint-satisfaction gaps that need better algorithms.

papers.title: Benchmarking Reward Hack Detection in Code Environments via Contrastive Analysis
papers.contribution: Building on this insight, we demonstrate that state-of-the-art models struggle significantly more with semantically contextualized reward hacks compared to syntactically contextualized ones

papers.title: Benchmarking the Limits of In-Context Reinforcement Learning for Ad-Hoc Teamwork
papers.contribution: Evaluation reveals that representative ICRL algorithms (AD, DPT) fail to exhibit robust test-time adaptation in multi-agent settings, underperforming random baselines across unseen teammates and layouts.

papers.title: Beyond a Million Tokens: Benchmarking and Enhancing Long-Term Memory in LLMs
papers.contribution: BEAM shows 1M-token context models struggle as dialogues lengthen; LIGHT consistently improves performance 3.5%-12.69% across various models by implementing long-term episodic, short-term working, and scratchpad memory.

papers.title: BioProBench: A Corpus and Benchmark for Biological Protocol Reasoning in Autonomous Science
papers.contribution: Comprehensive evaluation of 10 mainstream LLMs reveals significant performance drops on tasks demanding deep reasoning and quantitative precision; ProAgent substantially advances state-of-the-art in procedural reasoning for biology.

papers.title: CaReBench: A Fine-grained Benchmark for Video Captioning and Retrieval
papers.contribution: Develops a unified multimodal language model baseline using two-stage supervised fine-tuning that achieves competitive performance on both fine-grained video retrieval and detailed video captioning tasks.

papers.title: Can LLMs Move Beyond Short Exchanges to Realistic Therapy Conversations?
papers.contribution: Evaluating 18 LLMs reveals consistent gaps: high public QA scores degrade under expert rephrasing, dialogue competence falls below human clinical standards.

papers.title: Characterizing Deep Research: A Benchmark and Formal Definition
papers.contribution: Evaluates state-of-the-art DR systems, showing OpenAI's model performs best with F1 score of 0.55.

papers.title: CoNavBench: Collaborative Long-Horizon Vision-Language Navigation Benchmark
papers.contribution: Provides 4,048 single and collaborative episodes with a collaboration type taxonomy and a collaborative baseline using finetuned Qwen2.5-VL-3B that demonstrates collaborative policies reduce makespan.

papers.title: Completing Missing Annotation: Multi-Agent Debate for Accurate and Scalable Relevant Assessment for IR Benchmarks
papers.contribution: Achieves 95.2% labeling accuracy with only 3.5% human involvement and identifies 29,824 missing relevant chunks, showing that unlabeled data distorts retriever rankings.

papers.title: Credit-Budgeted ICPC-Style Coding: When LLM Agents Must Pay for Every Decision
papers.contribution: Exposes hidden costs and ROI of different agent strategies, demonstrating rich policy space where identical models diverge in self-play depending on risk/budget trade-offs.

papers.title: CyberGym-E2E: Scalable Real-World Benchmark for AI Agents' End-to-End Cybersecurity Capabilities
papers.contribution: CyberGym-E2E provides large-scale benchmark of 920 real-world vulnerabilities across 139 projects for comprehensive evaluation of AI agents' cybersecurity capabilities.

papers.title: CyberGym: Evaluating AI Agents' Real-World Cybersecurity Capabilities at Scale
papers.contribution: Top-performing agents achieve ~20% success rate, discovered 35 zero-day vulnerabilities and identified 17 historically incomplete patches, demonstrating both benchmark rigor and real-world security impact.

papers.title: DV-World: Benchmarking Data Visualization Agents in Real-World Scenarios
papers.contribution: Shows state-of-the-art models achieve below 50% overall performance, exposing major gaps in real-world data visualization capabilities.

papers.title: DevOps-Gym: Benchmarking AI Agents in Software DevOps Cycle
papers.contribution: State-of-the-art models achieve only around 15% success on new tasks like monitoring, highlighting fundamental limitations in automating the full DevOps cycle.

papers.title: EvoClaw: Evaluating AI Agents on Continuous Software Evolution
papers.contribution: Evaluation of 12 frontier models reveals critical vulnerability: performance drops from >80% on isolated tasks to at most 38% in continuous evolution, exposing agents' struggle with long-term maintenance.

papers.title: Expanding the Capability Frontier of LLM Agents with ZPD-Guided Data Synthesis
papers.contribution: AgentFrontier-30B-A3B achieves state-of-the-art on Humanity's Last Exam, outperforming leading proprietary agents by leveraging ZPD-guided synthesis.

papers.title: ExpertLongBench: Benchmarking Language Models on Expert-Level Long-Form Generation Tasks with Structured Checklists
papers.contribution: Shows top performer (Gemini-2.5-Pro) achieves only 33.4 F1 score, revealing significant room for improvement on expert-level tasks.

papers.title: FeatureBench: Benchmarking Agentic Coding for Complex Feature Development
papers.contribution: FeatureBench curates 200 challenging tasks and 3825 executable environments from 24 repositories; state-of-the-art Claude 4.5 Opus achieves 11.0% success rate compared to 74.4% on SWE-bench.

papers.title: FrontierCO: Real-World and Large-Scale Evaluation of Machine Learning Solvers for Combinatorial Optimization
papers.contribution: Evaluates 16 ML solvers against classical solvers, finding persistent performance gaps that widen under structural challenges and large scales like TSP up to 10M nodes.

papers.title: GIQ: Benchmarking 3D Geometric Reasoning of Vision Foundation Models with Simulated and Real Polyhedra
papers.contribution: Reveals significant shortcomings: SOTA algorithms struggle reconstructing basic geometric forms; VLMs falter on tasks requiring detailed geometric differentiation.

papers.title: GeoGramBench: Benchmarking the Geometric Program Reasoning in Modern LLMs
papers.contribution: Evaluation of 17 frontier LLMs reveals consistent deficiencies, with even the most advanced models achieving less than 50% accuracy at the highest abstraction level.

papers.title: Grounding Computer Use Agents on Human Demonstrations
papers.contribution: GroundNext achieves state-of-the-art results on five grounding benchmarks using less than one-tenth the training data of prior work.

papers.title: HARDTESTGEN: A High-Quality RL Verifier Generation Pipeline for LLM Algorithimic Coding
papers.contribution: Test verifiers achieve 11.22 percentage points higher precision than existing tests, and downstream RL training with these tests improves LLM code generation performance.

papers.title: HUME: Measuring the Human-Model Performance Gap in Text Embedding Tasks
papers.contribution: Humans achieve 77.6% average performance versus 80.1% for best models, with LLM annotators reaching only 76.1%, revealing substantial variation across datasets and languages.

papers.title: How Reliable is Language Model Micro-Benchmarking?
papers.contribution: The work shows that no micro-benchmarking method can consistently rank models 3.5 points apart on MMLU-Pro or 4 points on BIG-Bench Hard, requiring up to 250 examples for reliable comparisons.

papers.title: Human Behavior Atlas: Benchmarking Unified Psychological And Social Behavior Understanding
papers.contribution: Training on the benchmark enables models (Omnisapiens-7B variants) to outperform multimodal LLMs and improve transfer to novel behavioral datasets.

papers.title: InteractBench: Benchmarking LLMs on Competitive Programming under Unrevealed Information
papers.contribution: Reveals significant interaction gap with advanced reasoning models achieving limited success, proposing fine-grained failure taxonomy showing protocol violations and query-budget overruns are frequent despite algorithmic logic errors remaining dominant.

papers.title: JailNewsBench: Multi-Lingual and Regional Benchmark for Fake News Generation under Jailbreak Attacks
papers.contribution: Evaluates 9 LLMs revealing maximum attack success of 86.3% and harmfulness score 3.5/5, with defensive performance significantly higher for English than other regions.

papers.title: Kaleidoscope: In-language Exams for Massively Multilingual Vision Evaluation
papers.contribution: Demonstrates that multilingual VLMs perform poorly on low-resource languages and complex multimodal scenarios, highlighting need for culturally inclusive evaluation.

papers.title: LALM-as-a-Judge: Benchmarking Large Audio-Language Models for Safety Evaluation in Multi-Turn Spoken Dialogues
papers.contribution: Shows audio contributes non-lexical evidence beyond transcripts; multimodal gains vary with audio-pathway bottlenecks; derives practitioner guidance for LALM deployment.

papers.title: LOCA-bench: Benchmarking Language Agents Under Controllable and Extreme Context Growth
papers.contribution: First benchmark for language agents under long-context conditions; shows advanced context-management techniques substantially improve success rates.

papers.title: LOVE: Benchmarking and Evaluating Text-to-Video Generation and Video-to-Text Interpretation
papers.contribution: LOVE achieves state-of-the-art performance on AIGV evaluation across multiple dimensions; LOVE-Reward significantly improves video generation quality via reinforcement learning.

papers.title: Large Language Models as Topological Thinkers: A Benchmark on Graph Persistent Homology
papers.contribution: Provides first in-depth view of LLMs' ability to bridge discrete graph structures with topological abstraction.

papers.title: LitReview Arena: Evaluating Literature Review Agents with Battle-style Peer Review Platform
papers.contribution: From this protocol, we collect 3k expert judgments, each containing five dimension-wise outcomes, and show that even the strongest current systems win only 23

papers.title: LiveClin: A Live Clinical Benchmark without Leakage
papers.contribution: Benchmark of 1,407 case reports and 6,605 questions revealing top model achieves only 35.7% case accuracy, with Chief Physicians outperforming most models, providing a continuously evolving evaluation framework.

papers.title: MCP Security Bench (MSB): Benchmarking Attacks Against Model Context Protocol in LLM Agents
papers.contribution: MSB evaluates 9 LLM agents across 405 tools with 2,000 attack instances, revealing vulnerability patterns and introducing Net Resilient Performance (NRP) to quantify the security-performance tradeoff.

papers.title: MCP-Bench: Benchmarking Tool-Using LLM Agents with Complex Real-World Tasks via MCP Servers
papers.contribution: Experiments on 20 advanced LLMs reveal persistent challenges in tool-level schema understanding, trajectory planning, and cross-domain task completion.

papers.title: MEAL: A Benchmark for Continual Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning
papers.contribution: Discovers failure modes in long task sequences not apparent at smaller scales; first benchmark for continual multi-agent RL.

papers.title: MGAL: A Multilingual Granularity-Aware Long-Context Benchmark
papers.contribution: Reveals that LLMs perform well at word-level tasks but struggle with coarser granularities, and identifies new challenges including local semantic crowding and fluency-consistency gaps.

papers.title: MME-Emotion: A Holistic Evaluation Benchmark for Emotional Intelligence in Multimodal Large Language Models
papers.contribution: Evaluation of 20 advanced MLLMs reveals unsatisfactory emotional intelligence with the best achieving only 39.3% recognition and 56.0% Chain-of-Thought scores.

papers.title: MORE: A Multilingual Document Parsing Benchmark and Evaluation
papers.contribution: Establishes new performance baselines for long-tail languages and validates benchmark effectiveness in diagnosing model capabilities on realistic scenarios.

papers.title: Moving Beyond Medical Exams: A Clinician-Annotated Fairness Dataset of Real-World Tasks and Ambiguity in Mental Healthcare
papers.contribution: The dataset enables systematic fairness evaluation across 16 off-the-shelf and 6 health-tuned LMs, revealing how demographic factors affect model decision-making in mental health.

papers.title: NewtonBench: Benchmarking Generalizable Scientific Law Discovery in LLM Agents
papers.contribution: Frontier models show fragile discovery capability degrading with system complexity and noise; code interpreters can hinder capable models via premature exploitation.

papers.title: OSIRIS: Bridging Analog Circuit Design and Machine Learning with Scalable Dataset Generation
papers.contribution: Releases a dataset of 87,100 circuit variations and provides an RL-based baseline method, enabling machine learning approaches to analog design automation.

papers.title: OSWorld-MCP: Benchmarking MCP Tool Invocation In Computer-Use Agents
papers.contribution: Evaluations show that MCP tools improve task success rates (8.3% to 20.4% for o3, 40.1% to 43.3% for Claude 4 Sonnet) but models underutilize them (only 36.3% tool invocation rate).

papers.title: Omni-iEEG: A Large-Scale, Comprehensive iEEG Dataset and Benchmark for Epilepsy Research
papers.contribution: Provides 302-patient, 178-hour resource with clinically meaningful tasks and unified evaluation metrics enabling systematic model assessment.

papers.title: PLANETALIGN: A Comprehensive Python Library for Benchmarking Network Alignment
papers.contribution: Comprehensive comparative studies reveal practical insights into existing NA methods' strengths and limitations, facilitating more effective and robust method development.

papers.title: POEMetric: The Last Stanza of Humanity
papers.contribution: All models fail to reach human-level advanced abilities; top LLMs achieve 3.20 overall poem quality versus humans' 4.22, with humans excelling at creativity (4.02) and imagery (4.49).

papers.title: PluriHarms: Benchmarking the Full Spectrum of Human Judgments on AI Harm
papers.contribution: Demonstrates that personalization significantly improves prediction of human harm judgments and reveals that imminent risks, tangible harms, and annotator traits (toxicity experience, education) systematically explain disagreement.

papers.title: ProOPF: Benchmarking and Improving LLMs for Professional-Grade Power Systems Optimization Modeling
papers.contribution: Provides professional-grade dataset and benchmark for evaluating LLMs on rigorous OPF modeling.

papers.title: QEDBench: Quantifying the Alignment Gap in Automated Evaluation of University-Level Mathematical Proofs
papers.contribution: Reveals frontier evaluators like Claude 4.5 Opus exhibit positive bias up to +0.28, while specialized reasoning models like o3-deep-research collapse in discrete domains (42.1% accuracy in Graph Theory vs 0.91 for generalists.

papers.title: QiMeng-LibBench: Benchmarking LLM Agents for Library-Scale Cross-Architecture Migration
papers.contribution: Evaluation reveals agents achieve only 20.88% correctness due to pattern matching; FSCM improves OpenCV correctness to 71%.

papers.title: SCUBA: Salesforce Computer Use Benchmark
papers.contribution: Reveals huge performance gaps: open-source models have <5% success vs closed-source 39% zero-shot; demonstration-augmentation improves to 50% success.

papers.title: SimuHome: A Temporal- and Environment-Aware Benchmark for Smart Home LLM Agents
papers.contribution: The main bottlenecks for developing smart home agents with such capabilities include the lack of a realistic simulation environment where agents can interact with devices and observe the results, as w

papers.title: Stability Under Scrutiny: Benchmarking Representation Paradigms for Online HD Mapping
papers.contribution: Analysis of 42 models shows accuracy and stability are largely independent dimensions, and identifies architectural factors contributing to both.

papers.title: StarEmbed: Benchmarking Time Series Foundation Models on Astronomical Observations of Variable Stars
papers.contribution: Demonstrates that Chronos achieves state-of-the-art clustering and OOD detection on light curves despite non-astronomical pre-training, establishing a pathway toward universal light curve embeddings.

papers.title: TCD-Arena: Assessing Robustness of Time Series Causal Discovery Methods Against Assumption Violations
papers.contribution: The extensive empirical study reveals nuanced robustness profiles for 27 distinct assumption violations and shows CD ensembles can boost general robustness.

papers.title: TTSDS2: Resources and Benchmark for Evaluating Human-Quality Text to Speech Systems
papers.contribution: TTSDS2 achieves Spearman correlation above 0.50 for every domain and subjective score across 16 compared metrics, with resources including a multilingual dataset and a pipeline avoiding data leakage.

papers.title: TelecomTS: A Multi-Modal Observability Dataset for Time Series and Language Analysis
papers.contribution: Benchmarking state-of-the-art models reveals existing approaches struggle with abrupt, noisy, high-variance dynamics, emphasizing need for foundation time series models natively leveraging scale information.

papers.title: TestExplora: Benchmarking LLMs for Proactive Bug Discovery via Repository-Level Test Generation
papers.contribution: Achieves maximum Fail-to-Pass (F2P) rate of 16.06%, revealing significant capability gap, with SWEAgent achieving 17.27% F2P and 29.7% F2P@5.

papers.title: The Decrypto Benchmark for Multi-Agent Reasoning and Theory of Mind
papers.contribution: LLMs lag behind humans on key game metrics, and reasoning models are significantly worse at ToM tasks than older counterparts, revealing critical gaps.

papers.title: VLA-Arena: An Open-Source Framework for Benchmarking Vision-Language-Action Models
papers.contribution: Evaluation of state-of-the-art VLAs reveals critical limitations including memorization over generalization, superficial visual perception, and neglect of safety constraints, with model rank reversals validating non-redundant difficulty levels.

papers.title: Virne: A Comprehensive Benchmark for RL-based Network Resource Allocation in NFV
papers.contribution: Enables comprehensive analysis through diverse simulations, rich implementations, and thorough evaluation providing insights into performance tradeoffs.

papers.title: Virtual Community: An Open World for Humans, Robots, and Society
papers.contribution: Virtual Community enables two novel challenges: Community Planning Challenge for multi-agent reasoning and Community Robot Challenge for multi-robot collaboration, with evaluation of baseline approaches.

papers.title: VisioMath: Benchmarking Figure-based Mathematical Reasoning in LMMs
papers.contribution: Benchmark reveals consistent accuracy decline as inter-image similarity increases; alignment-oriented training strategies achieve substantial accuracy gains.

papers.title: VitaBench: Benchmarking LLM Agents with Versatile Interactive Tasks in Real-world Applications
papers.contribution: State-of-the-art models achieve only 30% success on cross-scenario tasks and less than 50% on single-scenario tasks, revealing benchmark's challenge.

papers.title: WARC-Bench: Web Archive based Benchmark for GUI Subtask Executions
papers.contribution: SFT achieves 48.8% success rate; RLVR over SFT improves to 52.8%, outperforming many frontier models on critical web navigation subtasks.

papers.title: WebDevJudge: Evaluating (M)LLMs as Critiques for Web Development Quality
papers.contribution: Experiments reveal a significant gap between LLM judges and human experts, with failures in recognizing functional equivalence, verifying task feasibility, and mitigating bias.

papers.title: WideSearch: Benchmarking Agentic Broad Info-Seeking
papers.contribution: Benchmarking 10+ agentic systems reveals most achieve near 0% success with the best reaching 7%, demonstrating critical deficiencies in large-scale information seeking.

papers.title: WorldSense: Evaluating Real-world Omnimodal Understanding for Multimodal LLMs
papers.contribution: Demonstrates that existing models achieve only 65.1% best accuracy on real-world omni-modal understanding tasks across 1,662 audio-visual videos.
